I will do it mostly the way that has kept my land steady, then make small adjustments from what I saw in recent years. On my 5.2 mu, wheat and maize are one set of land, just winter wheat first and summer maize after it, so I count the full 5.2 mu for both crops. I have farmed a long time, so I do not like making big changes all at once. If fertilizer is short, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because around here the better-performing varieties are already common and I have seen they stand better and yield better than old seed. For wheat, I will put the base fertilizer down before sowing, then give nitrogen again at greening or jointing, and with well water I will irrigate about 3 times if the year is normal. For maize after wheat harvest, I will sow quickly, use enough nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer hard, and give 2 irrigations if rain is not enough. I will keep rotary tillage because my land is not large, it saves labor, and it works well enough for my wheat-maize rotation. I will spray when needed, usually 2 times on wheat and 2 times on maize in a normal year. I am not chasing the fanciest method. I will spend where it protects yield and keep the rest simple so the whole season stays manageable for a two-person household.
